evidence.quote: Medulla oblongata | Myelencephalon (fifth vesicle)
the myelencephalon (fifth vesicle)

definitions.text: The most caudal tip of the fourth ventricle.

evidence.quote: The obex is the most caudal tip of the fourth ventricle
The peak is the fastigium; the caudal tip the obex

definitions.text: The third cranial nerve, which exits the anterior surface of the midbrain between the cerebral peduncles.

evidence.quote: The oculomotor nerve (CN III) is seen exiting from between the peduncles
Anterior, midbrain | III between the cerebral peduncles

definitions.text: The first cranial nerve; one of the two cranial nerves that do not arise from the brainstem.

evidence.quote: with the exception of two: the optic nerve and the olfactory nerve
All cranial nerves arise from the brainstem except the optic and olfactory nerves

definitions.text: An elevation on the medulla lying lateral to the pyramid, produced by the inferior olivary nucleus.

evidence.quote: the olive lateral to it by the inferior olivary nucleus
An elevation, lies lateral to the pyramid. Produced by inferior olivary nucleus

definitions.text: The second cranial nerve, running from the eye to the optic chiasm; one of the two cranial nerves that do not arise from the brainstem.

evidence.quote: with the exception of two: the optic nerve and the olfactory nerve
Ten of twelve cranial nerves arise from it; not CN I or II

title: Paramedian position of the vocal cord
subject: subj:anat3

definitions.text: A position of the vocal cord between abduction and adduction, in which the cord of the affected side lies and does not vibrate after damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: Unilateral recurrent nerve palsy: paramedian cord.
lies in paramedian position (between ‘abduction and adduction) and does not vibrate
the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position, between abduction and adduction, and does not vibrate

definitions.text: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy. The sound produced is then modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants.

evidence.quote: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy
The phonation (speech) is produced by the vibrations of the vocal cords

definitions.text: The middle and largest part of the brainstem, derived from the metencephalon with the cerebellum. Its ventral bulge, about 2.5 cm, is made by transverse pontocerebellar fibres, and CN V to VIII are associated with it.

evidence.quote: The largest part, from the metencephalon with the cerebellum
Pons: largest; basilar artery in the basilar groove; CN V to VIII
The anterior or ventral surface of the pons is marked by a bulging formed by the transverse pontocerebellar fibres

definitions.text: The angle between the lower border of the pons and the superior border of the medulla, an important landmark where CN VI, VII and VIII emerge from medial to lateral.

evidence.quote: The pontomedullary junction is an important anatomical landmark defined by the angle between the lower border of the pons and the superior border of the medulla
VI, VII, VIII at the pontomedullary junction (medial to lateral)

definitions.text: The cranial fossa in which the brainstem lies, on the clivus and under the tentorium cerebelli.

evidence.quote: It lies in the posterior cranial fossa, on the clivus, under the tentorium cerebelli
It lies at the cerebral posterior fossa, on the basilar part of occipital bone (clivus)

definitions.text: The intrinsic muscle that is the only dilator of the glottis and the only abductor of the vocal cords, inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid. It is called the safety muscle of the larynx: if it is paralysed the adductors take the upper hand and the person might die from lack of air.

evidence.quote: Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx.
Dilator of the glottis: the posterior cricoarytenoid, the only one.
If posterior cricoarytenoids are paralyzed, the adductor ‘muscles (of vocal cords) take the upper hand and the person might die due to lack of air

definitions.text: A branch of the inferior thyroid artery that supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa and anastomoses with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery. Supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa
Posteroinferior Laryngeal Artery (ALPI): branch of the Inferior Thyroid Artery. It vascularizes the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa

definitions.text: An elevation on either side of the ventral median fissure of the medulla, produced by the corticospinal tract.

evidence.quote: The pyramid on each side is made by the corticospinal tract
An elevation, lies on either (lateral)side of ventral median fissure Produced by corticospinal tract

definitions.text: The crossing of most corticospinal fibres, 75 to 90 percent, in the lower medulla, marking the lower part of the ventral median fissure.

evidence.quote: Its lower part is marked by decussation of most of pyramidal(corticospinal) fibers (75%-90%)
Pyramids = corticospinal tracts; 75-90% decussate in the lower medulla
the pyramids decussate in the medulla

definitions.text: A branch of the vagus arising on the right at the base of the neck and on the left in the thorax. It is motor to all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and sensory below the vocal folds. The left nerve loops under the aortic arch and the right under the subclavian artery.

evidence.quote: Motor to all the intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid; sensory below the vocal folds through an ascending branch anastomosing with the superior laryngeal nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid, and sensation below the cords.
The left recurrent nerve loops under the aortic arch (long course → more often damaged by chest disease); the right loops under the subclavian artery.

definitions.text: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy. Unilaterally, the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates; bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy: unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates
bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing
Unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy (thyroidectomy, left-sided aortic or lung lesions): hoarse voice, cord paramedian. Bilateral: stridor, airway emergency.

definitions.text: The centres for breathing and cardiovascular control, located in the medulla oblongata, which is why compression or a lesion of the medulla is life-threatening.

evidence.quote: the respiratory and cardiovascular centres are in the medulla
cardiovascular and respiratory centres (medulla)
The respiratory and cardiovascular centres are in the medulla, which is why medullary compression is life-threatening

definitions.text: A network of neuronal cell bodies and small axon bundles running in many directions, without distinct boundaries, spread from the spinal cord through the brainstem to the hypothalamus and thalamus. It integrates vital functions: arousal, consciousness, sleep-wake cycles, motor coordination, cardiovascular and respiratory control, pain modulation and habituation.

evidence.quote: It integrates vital functions: arousal, consciousness, sleep-wake cycles, motor coordination, cardiovascular and respiratory control, pain modulation and habituation
The reticular formation (RF) consists of an intricate mixture of neuronal cell bodies and fascicles of axons running in small bundles
Reticular formation: consciousness, sleep, breathing, heart rate, pain

definitions.text: The diamond-shaped depression on the dorsal surface of the pons and upper half of the medulla that forms the floor of the fourth ventricle.

evidence.quote: formed by the rhomboid fossa, a diamond-shaped depression on the dorsal surface of the pons and upper half of the medulla
fourth ventricle floor is the rhomboid fossa

definitions.text: The opening between the vocal cords, through which air passes when the cords are abducted.

evidence.quote: abduct the vocal cords, letting air through the rima glottidis
The gap between the vocal cords

definitions.text: An ascending unconscious tract through the brainstem carrying proprioception to the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Spinocerebellar | Ascending, unconscious | Proprioception to the cerebellum
Unconscious tracts : comprised of the spinocerebellar tracts

title: Stria medullaris of the fourth ventricle
subject: subj:anat3

definitions.text: A bundle of nerve fibres crossing the floor of the fourth ventricle transversely from the lateral aspect into the midline, marking the posterior border between the pons and the medulla.

evidence.quote: The stria medullaris of the fourth ventricle is a bundle of nerve fibres crossing transversely from the lateral aspect into the midline
the stria medullaris marking the pons-medulla border

definitions.text: The cerebellar peduncle that connects the midbrain with the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Superior peduncle connects midbrain with cerebellum
Cerebellar peduncles: superior to midbrain, middle to pons, inferior to medulla

definitions.text: One of the upper pair of rounded prominences of the tectum on the back of the midbrain, linked with the retina by the superior brachium and concerned with vision.

evidence.quote: The superior brachium links the superior colliculus with the retina (vision)
The upper pair of bumps on the back of the midbrain: visual reflexes

definitions.text: A branch of the superior thyroid artery that supplies the supraglottic part of the larynx and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery. It enters the larynx through the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the supraglottic part and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery
Superior Laryngeal Artery (SLA): branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the supraglottic part

definitions.text: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, that descends against the pharyngeal wall and divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into an internal and an external branch.

evidence.quote: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, descending against the pharyngeal wall and dividing behind the greater horn of the hyoid
It divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into two branches

definitions.text: The brachium extending laterally from the superior colliculus that forms a pathway between the superior colliculus and the retina, for vision.

evidence.quote: Superior quadrigeminal brachium forms a pathway between the superior colliculus and the retina of the eye( vision)
The superior brachium links the superior colliculus with the retina (vision)

definitions.text: The artery that gives off the superior laryngeal artery and the anteroinferior laryngeal artery to the larynx.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery
Anteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery

definitions.text: The compartment of the larynx above the glottis, comprising the vestibule, the laryngeal ventricle and the interarytenoid region. It is very rich in lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Supraglottic | Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords

definitions.text: An air cavity above the larynx, notably the pharynx and the oral cavity, that modifies and filters the laryngeal sound by resonance, enriching some frequencies and suppressing others, and takes part in articulation.

evidence.quote: The sound produced is immediately modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants: the bucco-pharyngeal resonators
Filter role: resonance and enrichment of certain frequencies or suppression of others, with two areas of particular enhancement, the pharynx and the oral cavity

definitions.text: The part of the midbrain behind the cerebral aqueduct, housing four colliculi, two superior and two inferior, just below the pineal gland.

evidence.quote: Tectum, behind the cerebral aqueduct: two superior and two inferior colliculi below the pineal gland
The tectum houses four rounded prominences named colliculi which sit directly inferior to the pineal gland

definitions.text: The opening in the tentorium cerebelli, also called the foramen of Pacchioni, through which the midbrain passes.

evidence.quote: passing through the tentorial opening (foramen of Pacchioni)
the opening in the tentorium cerebelli: foramen of PACCHIONNI

definitions.text: The structure under which the brainstem lies in the posterior cranial fossa; the midbrain travels through its opening.

evidence.quote: on the clivus, under the tentorium cerebelli
It travels through the opening in the tentorium cerebelli

definitions.text: A structure belonging to the diencephalon; it is not part of the brainstem.

evidence.quote: The thalamus is NOT brainstem
the thalamus is not part of the brainstem
The thalamus belongs to the diencephalon

definitions.text: An intrinsic muscle of the larynx listed among the constrictors of the glottis, with a superior part running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid and an inferior part, the vocal muscle. It relaxes the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Relax the vocal cords | Thyroarytenoid
superior thyroarytenoid (from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid)
Thyroarytenoid: relaxes the vocal cords

definitions.text: An extrinsic ligament of the larynx that attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle.

evidence.quote: Thyroepiglottic ligament: attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle
inferior inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament

definitions.text: An extrinsic membrane of the larynx running from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone, with a medial and two lateral thickenings. It is pierced by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve together with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Thyrohyoid membrane: from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone
The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve pierces it with the superior laryngeal artery

definitions.text: A large unpaired cartilage of the larynx shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae. Its thick posterior margin is extended by superior and inferior cornua, the inferior carrying a cricoid articular surface.

evidence.quote: Shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae
Three unpaired and large: thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis

definitions.text: An operation, named in the lecture as partial thyroidectomy, during which the recurrent laryngeal nerve is often damaged accidentally.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy

definitions.text: The tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid, lying below the larynx and joined to the cricoid by the cricotracheal ligament.

evidence.quote: Trachea: the tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid.
The cricotracheal ligament runs between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring

definitions.text: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, also called the interarytenoid. It inserts on the posterior side of the arytenoid cartilage and adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Transverse arytenoid is the only unpaired intrinsic muscle.
the posterior side takes the transverse arytenoid muscle
Transverse arytenoid: adduct the vocal cords.

definitions.text: The fissure by which the brainstem is connected above to the diencephalon; the upper limit of the brainstem.

evidence.quote: Above, the diencephalon by the transverse fissure of Bichat
Above: diencephalon by transverse fissure of BICHAT

definitions.text: The fifth cranial nerve, a large nerve that emerges from the lateral aspect of the mid-pons.

evidence.quote: CN V, trigeminal | Lateral mid-pons
Cranial nerve V: trigeminal originates from the lateral aspect of mid pons

definitions.text: The fourth cranial nerve, which emerges below the colliculi from the dorsal surface of the midbrain; it is the only cranial nerve emerging dorsally.

evidence.quote: the trochlear nerve (cranial nerve IV), which emerges from the dorsal surface of the midbrain
CN IV is the only nerve emerging dorsally
Inferior to the colliculi, the trochlear nerve (CN IV) emerges before sweeping across to the anterior surface

definitions.text: The tenth cranial nerve, one of the mixed nerves, which leaves the medulla behind the olive, below the glossopharyngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: Lateral, behind the olive | IX, X and XI, the mixed nerves
Leaves the medulla behind the olive, below IX
X the vagus nerve

definitions.text: The nerve whose branches, the superior laryngeal nerve and the recurrent laryngeal nerve, innervate the larynx.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal nerve | A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory
From the vagus, on the right at the base of the neck and on the left at the thorax

definitions.text: The midline fissure on the ventral surface of the medulla, continuous with that of the spinal cord, which divides the medulla into two halves; its lower part is marked by the decussation of most corticospinal fibres.

evidence.quote: Continuation of ventral median fissure of spinal cord. Divides the medulla into 2 halves
The ventral median fissure, continuous with the cord's, is marked below by the decussation of 75 to 90 percent of corticospinal fibres

definitions.text: The false vocal cord or ventricular band. The vestibule lies above the vestibular folds and the laryngeal ventricle lies between them and the vocal folds.

evidence.quote: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
vestibule above the vestibular folds, ventricle between them and the vocal folds

definitions.text: An intrinsic ligament of the larynx, tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid.

evidence.quote: The vestibular ligament is tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid

definitions.text: The eighth cranial nerve, which emerges lateral to the facial nerve at the cerebellopontine angle.

evidence.quote: CN VIII, vestibulocochlear | Lateral to CN VII
Cranial nerve VIII: vestibulocochlear originates laterally to the facial nerve

title: Vibratory cycle of the vocal folds
subject: subj:anat3

definitions.text: The three-step cycle of phonation: the folds close as the arytenoids come together (phonatory position); they open when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, letting a puff of air pass at high speed as an acoustic impulse; then the folds close again.

evidence.quote: Putting into phonatory position: the folds close as the arytenoids come together
when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, a puff of air passes at high speed, an acoustic impulse

definitions.text: One of two pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle. The vocal cords are covered by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium and have no lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Two pearly white vocal cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle
Vocal cords have stratified squamous epithelium and no lymphatics.
Vocal cords: 2 pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid cartilage in back

definitions.text: The movement that opens the vocal cords and lets air through the rima glottidis. It is produced only by the posterior cricoarytenoids: the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening.

evidence.quote: When they contract, the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening
Abduct the vocal cords | Posterior cricoarytenoids

definitions.text: The movement that brings the vocal cords together, produced by the lateral cricoarytenoids and the transverse arytenoid. The cords are kept adducted for phonation.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
The vocal cords are kept adducted

definitions.text: The tensing or relaxing of the vocal cords. The cricothyroid and vocalis tense them, as does tilting of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint; the thyroarytenoid relaxes them.

evidence.quote: Tense: cricothyroid and vocalis. Relax: thyroarytenoid.
Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis (arch up, lamina down) tenses the vocal cords

definitions.text: An intrinsic ligament of the larynx formed by the cricothyroid ligament stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process of the arytenoid. Together with muscle it makes up the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
made of vocal ligament and muscle

definitions.text: An inflammatory nodule that develops in people who overuse the voice at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the vocal cords, the area of maximum contact during vibration. The nodules are bilateral and symmetrical, pin head to split pea in size, soft, reddish and oedematous early and later greyish or whitish.

evidence.quote: The area of maximum contact during vibration is at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the cords
Vocal nodules form at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two thirds of the cords.
the inflammatory nodules develop at these sites called vocal nodules

definitions.text: The extension of the anterior angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, which gives insertion to the vocal ligament.

evidence.quote: The anterior angle of the base extends as the vocal process (insertion of the vocal ligament)
The vocal process gives insertion to the : • Vocal ligament

definitions.text: The inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle, running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid. It tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle (from the reentrant angle to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid), which tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the cord
Tense the vocal cords | Cricothyroid, vocalis
